newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba calls parliamentary session for July.
newsitem.headline: Cuba calls parliamentary session for July.

text.p: Cuba's National Assembly, which sits for two sessions a year each lasting a couple of days, will hold the first session of 1997 in July, officials said on Wednesday.
Assembly president Ricardo Alarcon said in a statement in the ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma that the assembly would convene on July 11. It did not say what issues would be discussed.

The assembly held just one session last year, at the end of December, to hear reports on the economy, approve the budget for this year and pass legislation aimed at countering the U.S. Helms-Burton law against Cuba.
